## Context / Problem
Most core ticket, store, read/write, config, import/export, maintenance, and gate commands parse argv imperatively. Adding docs-only argparse definitions would create the duplicate grammar RP-05 is meant to eliminate.

## Approach
Inventory every registered core grammar owned by `src/rebar/_commands/`, `src/rebar/_engine_support/`, and `src/rebar/_io/`, PLUS the two consumers that make a migrated grammar live: the per-`Route` `parser_factory` field in `src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py` (core Routes in `_reads_init_only`/`_simple_read_groups`/`_lifecycle`/`_writes_full`/`_bridge_and_arms` currently carry NO `parser_factory`; only advanced/intercept routes set it) and the runtime handler switch in `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` (the `_dispatch_*` family, which selects and invokes each command's handler). For each command:

1. Capture current production-path positive, negative, boundary, surplus/missing argument, option-space/equal, global-output, and `--` behavior from existing tests and focused additions.
2. Move the grammar into a side-effect-free factory in the new `src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/` package using the S2a argparse contract, extracting shared argument-definition helpers where canonical and compatibility forms overlap.
3. Switch the runtime handler to parse with that same factory in the same change, wiring the `parser_factory` reference onto the command's core `Route` in `_registry.py` and routing its `_dispatch_*` handler through that factory. Keep domain execution and initialization outside the parser module.
4. Preserve command-specific diagnostic text, stdout/stderr, and exit codes through the shared parser seam; do not accept an option merely because argparse can parse it.
5. Register the parser reference and prove only the selected parser/handler is resolved during execution (assert via a real production-path invocation that no unrelated parser factory or handler is constructed).

Cover the leaf positional registry, reads/lookups/gates, create/edit/lifecycle, compaction/fsck/doctor/maintenance, config, import/export, identity-adjacent core store commands, and static reads. EXCLUDE `metrics`: its route already carries `parser_factory="rebar._cli._parsers.advanced.metrics:build"` from S2c and is out of scope here (re-migrating it is forbidden). Split files only along existing command-family call graphs and respect module-size rules.

### Router global-flag/end-of-options seam (layering)
The router-level global extraction (`--output`/`-o`, `--quiet`, `--allow-secret-pattern`, applied to the pre-`--` segment only) runs in `_cli/__init__.py` BEFORE the per-command factory sees argv, exactly as today. Per-command factories parse only the command-local tail after that extraction; this ordering is invariant and no factory re-declares a global flag.

### Unknown-token semantics (per-family, preserved)
Core families currently have OPPOSITE unknown-token behavior: some parse via `parse_known_args` (silently skipping unknown tokens) while the positional-only leaf registry REJECTS stray option tokens with exit 2. Stock argparse reproduces neither by default. Each migrated factory MUST preserve its own family's pre-migration unknown-token semantics (skip vs reject-with-exit-2), proven by a negative test per semantics class; a family's semantics is not silently normalized to argparse's default.

## Compatibility and Rollback
No help cutover occurs here. Accepted grammar and execution behavior are invariant unless this ticket records and receives approval for a specific delta. A parser family, its `Route` `parser_factory` wiring, and its handler switch are ONE revertable unit; no stored data changes.

## Testing
Use the smallest production path crossing each parser. Pure parser tables may be unit-tested, but public oracles run real CLI subprocesses or existing interface tests and assert return code, exact relevant stream, parsed effect/persisted state, and unchanged state on refusal. Include nearest controls and verify tests run under `make test`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Every registered core command runtime (its `_dispatch_*` handler) calls its S2a parser factory via a `parser_factory` reference wired onto its core `Route` in `_registry.py`; no parallel imperative grammar remains for that command. `metrics` is excluded (already migrated in S2c).
- [x] Accepted/rejected argv matrices cover missing/surplus values, space/equal options, `--`, global confirmation/output extraction, per-family unknown-token semantics (skip vs reject-exit-2), and representative malformed input.
- [x] Existing persisted effects, no-effect refusals, diagnostics, streams, and exit codes show no unapproved behavior delta, verified through real production-path (subprocess/interface) tests.
- [x] Parser construction imports no domain executor or optional dependency, and a real selected execution resolves no unrelated parser factory or handler (proven by a construction-exclusion probe plus a dispatch-isolation assertion).
- [x] All touched modules meet module-size/complexity policy, and each family is proven revertable as one unit (parser factory + `Route` wiring + handler switch) — demonstrated by confirming the family's parser module, its single `_registry.py` wiring line, and its `_dispatch_*` switch form one self-contained hunk with no cross-family coupling.
